topics.title: Exporting an application, product Rule, or Ruleset using the Export wizard

elements.description: A Product Rule (RAP) is the migration manifest; its generated ZIP/JAR archive carries the selected contents. Use Packaging wizard and Preview to verify Rules, associated data and required dependencies. Standard platform assets usually already exist on the target. A data instance’s Ruleset association supports packaging, not runtime access control. Accessible imported Rules may execute before the whole import finishes.

elements.text: Worked example: A data instance associated with Lending is easier to include in its package, but this association does not prevent another application from accessing it.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Exporting an application, product Rule, or Ruleset using the Export wizard

elements.description: Export scope can be application, Ruleset/version, Product or patch. Check in intended edits: a checked-out personal copy is not the exported version. Export the selected package and import it on the target. Inspect errors and Preview rather than assuming every required component is included. Production/delegated Rulesets may need explicit inclusion and permission to package unlocked versions.

elements.text: Worked example: To send a targeted release to QA, preview the Product, check in intended edits, export the archive and import it on the target. Check production Ruleset inclusion explicitly.

examPitfalls.title: Manifest vs file
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The Product Rule itself is the transported ZIP.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Rule defines contents; the generated archive carries them.

examPitfalls.title: Association vs security
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Ruleset association restricts data at runtime.

examPitfalls.title: Checked-out edits
examPitfalls.trapDescription: An export includes the developer’s unsaved personal change.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check in intended edits before export.

practiceQuiz.scenario: QA requests a precisely selected set of Rules and associated configuration. What defines the migration contents?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Product Rule is the package manifest.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Product Rule. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: A template describes circumstance properties, not package contents.
optionExplanations.B: The Product Rule selects the components to migrate.
optionExplanations.C: Confidence is learning data, not a migration manifest.
optionExplanations.D: Urgency prioritizes work, not exported components.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer exports while the intended fix is checked out. Which version is included?

options.text: The stored original, not the checked-out edit

practiceQuiz.rationale: Check in intended edits before creating the archive.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Exporting an application, product Rule, or Ruleset using the Export wizard. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: The personal edit must be checked in first.
optionExplanations.B: Export does not automatically include both copies.
optionExplanations.C: The shared original is exported; the checked-out change is excluded.
optionExplanations.D: One checkout does not make every other rule unexportable.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO statements about data-to-Ruleset association are correct?

options.text: It grants runtime access only to that application
It does not restrict runtime behavior
It turns data into a Rule

practiceQuiz.rationale: Association is a packaging aid rather than an authorization boundary.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Product Rule. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Association lets packaging include the corresponding data instances.
optionExplanations.B: Association alone is not an application access restriction.
optionExplanations.C: It is packaging metadata, not a runtime restriction.
optionExplanations.D: The associated instance remains data, not a rule.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A delegated production Ruleset must remain editable and be shipped. What packaging detail needs review?

options.text: Include production Rulesets and allow required unlocked versions

practiceQuiz.rationale: The archive must deliberately include the editable production assets.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Exporting an application, product Rule, or Ruleset using the Export wizard. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Deleting the container removes needed assets.
optionExplanations.B: Blocking rules prevents normal execution, not packaging errors.
optionExplanations.C: Renaming rules is unrelated to including editable assets.
optionExplanations.D: Explicit production inclusion and unlocked-version allowance preserve the delegated package.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which action catches missing contents before archive generation?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Preview exposes what the manifest will carry.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Product Rule. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Preview lets you inspect the selected archive contents.
optionExplanations.B: As-of conditions select time-based behavior, not package contents.
optionExplanations.C: Skimming consolidates versions, not the manifest review.
optionExplanations.D: Changing a Persona does not inspect migration contents.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Only one Ruleset version is needed for a component handoff. Which export scope fits?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Choose the narrow export scope matching the handoff.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Exporting an application, product Rule, or Ruleset using the Export wizard. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Exporting every application exceeds the requested handoff.
optionExplanations.B: Ruleset/version mode matches this component scope.
optionExplanations.C: The current date is not an export scope.
optionExplanations.D: An Access Group alone omits the requested Ruleset version.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Users already access a Ruleset being imported. Which risk should be planned for?

options.text: Rules can never run until manual activation
Imported Rules may execute before the full archive finishes
The archive becomes an Access Group

practiceQuiz.rationale: Partial import timing can expose incomplete dependencies.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Product Rule. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Already accessible imported rules can execute without a separate activation.
optionExplanations.B: Case locking is not the universal effect of importing rules.
optionExplanations.C: Early execution can encounter dependencies not yet imported.
optionExplanations.D: An archive contains components; it does not become an Access Group.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO items complete a migration workflow?

options.text: Import the archive on the target

practiceQuiz.rationale: Verify the manifest and perform the target import; exporting alone is incomplete.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Exporting an application, product Rule, or Ruleset using the Export wizard. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Checking the contents helps detect missing components before handoff.
optionExplanations.B: Standard platform assets are normally already installed on the destination.
optionExplanations.C: The target must import the archive to receive its contents.
optionExplanations.D: Export excludes personal checkout changes; check them in first.

quickRecap.value: Product Rule = manifest; generated ZIP/JAR = archive.
Packaging aid; does not grant or restrict runtime access.
Check in → choose scope → preview → export → import → verify.
Accessible imported Rules can execute before the import is complete.
